name: Babylon.js
role: Full web 3D engine with built-in PBR, post effects, physics and node materials
summary: WebGL2 and WebGPU engine driven from JavaScript or TypeScript. Ships PBR, glow and other post effects, physics plugins, an inspector and a node material editor in one package. In VCR it would render a scene per seek to a transparent canvas like Three.js. Distinguishing strength: the integrated feature set means fewer third-party parts to version-match.
use_when: Over Three.js when you want effects, physics and node materials in one first-party package
Visual node-based material authoring through the Node Material Editor
Scenes already authored in the Babylon Sandbox or its tooling
avoid_when: Reusing pmndrs postprocessing, drei or glTF tooling: Three.js
Small bundle for one hero object: Three.js or OGL
React is the app shell: React Three Fiber

evidence.result: babylonjs 9.35.0 UMD build (not @babylonjs/core). 90 distinct 1280x720 alpha frames at 30 fps; 90 distinct hashes; all shuffled hashes equal sequential in two runs; frame 45 alpha min 0 max 1. babylonjs UMD build, Playwright 1.64.1, Chromium 156.0.8078.4, Node 22.19.0; screenshot route. Contact sheet inspected.
evidence.scope: babylonjs 9.35.0 UMD, not @babylonjs/core: Scene, ArcRotateCamera, box/sphere/torus set from t, one render per seek; alpha PNG; macOS arm64 Chromium. No runRenderLoop, post, PBR, particles.

assessment.rationale: Frequent npm releases, latest Oct 2026; Apache-2.0; official site reachable. Batteries-included alternative to Three.js with a Node Material Editor, but a smaller ecosystem and no pmndrs tooling.
